title: Alignment stage idles about 7% of thread time
body:
On the mgy run the alignment branch reports 93.0% busy over 175.7 s at 48 threads. That is about 12 s of idle thread time, more than any serial item except the db write. The likely cause is imbalance at the tail. `search.rs` runs `par_chunks(100)` over seeds grouped by query, and threads wait while the last chunks finish.

## Proposal

Measure busy time against chunk size before changing anything. Smaller chunks, or seeds from different queries interleaved, would recover part of the idle time.

## Open

- This needs the 48-thread box.

notes.author: jackroddy/4125deb5
notes.text:
The 93.0% did not reproduce. On the 48-thread box at `bb3c392`, pinned to the 48 physical cores of NUMA node 0 at `-t 48`, the full run reported the alignment stage at 99.0% busy over 124.7 s. The inputs were the same as the 481.8 s run. I do not know how that run was placed on the box, so the difference cannot be put down to pinning or to the code that changed since `432ff65`.

I then swept the chunk size in `par_chunks` in `search.rs`, from a scratch build that reads it from an environment variable. Every run aligned the seeds saved by the full run, through `--seeds`, on the same pinned cores:

| chunk | alignment wall, s | busy |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 124.64 | 100.0% |
| 10 | 128.08 | 97.3% |
| 25 | 124.64 | 99.9% |
| 50 | 124.63 | 99.9% |
| 100 | 123.82 | 99.5% |
| 100, repeated | 125.34 | 99.4% |
| 400 | 128.44 | 97.1% |

The spread is 123.8 to 128.4 s. The two runs of chunk 100 differ by 1.5 s. Chunk size makes no difference I can separate from run-to-run noise. I see no reason to change the 100 in `search.rs`. Sorted `results.tbl` from chunks 1, 400 and the repeat of 100 match the first chunk-100 run byte for byte.

The logs are in `tmp-claude/2026-10-18-serial-overhead-48t/sweep` on `catalyst`.
